summary: Quinault Tribe land in Jefferson County WA; 60-ft Aermotor tower and ground cabin built in the 1940s and abandoned in 1962; sources disagree on what remains; permission required.

facts.design: 60-foot Aermotor steel tower with 7x7-foot metal cab, plus a small rectangular wooden ground cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned 1962; the Register says removed, but WillhiteWeb says the tower is still on the ground and Fire Lookout says ruins are still present

access.note: On Quinault Indian Reservation land; road access exists, but permission from the Quinault Tribe is required and access roads are signed no trespassing

visit.trail_note: Good gravel roads reach the site; permission from the Quinault Tribe required

events.note: Fire Lookout says built in the 1940, which may mean the decade or 1940; the Register and WillhiteWeb say the 1940s. Year shown (1940) is a placeholder from Fire Lookout's wording; the exact year is not confirmed
WillhiteWeb photo caption shows the lookout and cabin in 1955
Register photographs dated 7/8/2000 show the tower lying on its side, the cab on its side, and the cabin being torn apart by trees
WillhiteWeb says the lookout area was logged around 2016

corrections.why: The record says gone, but WillhiteWeb says the tower is still present on the ground and Fire Lookout says ruins are still present. The Register (2011) says removed, and its own 2000 photos show the tower on its side.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the tower and cabin are now removed. Fire Lookout says ruins remain, and WillhiteWeb says the tower is still on the ground after logging around 2016. The Register's own 2000 photos show the tower lying on its side. The story reports the disagreement and gives the latest sources' account.
The Register gives 480 ft (146 m), which matches the record's 146.3 m. Fire Lookout and WillhiteWeb give 435 feet. The story does not repeat the elevation.

notes_for_editor: Build date: the Register and WillhiteWeb say the 1940s; Fire Lookout says 'built in the 1940', which may mean the decade or 1940; the built event uses 1940 as a placeholder and the note says so. Staffing: no lookout or fire is named in any source read. The site is on Quinault tribal land with permission required; the story tells readers to ask the Quinault Tribe and does not encourage entry. WillhiteWeb's 'still on the ground' statement is undated but mentions 2016 logging, so it postdates 2016; the Register's 'now removed' is from its 2011 registration and conflicts with its own 2000 photos. Height_m 18.3 is the 60-foot tower height converted. The record's elevation 146.3 m matches the Register but the other two sources give 435 ft. Not used: a WillhiteWeb photo caption with a 1936 CCC date, which does not concern the lookout.
